messages:
Maya: Heads up, seeing a tail-latency spike for hosted inference in eu-west1. P50 fine, p99 jumping to ~2.8s since ~06:12 UTC.
Maya: Root cause looks correlated to node-gpu-42 in rack-7. Dashboard shows temperature oscillations and short power dips.
infra-bot: [ALERT] node-gpu-42 sensor-failover detected: ambient_sensor -> fallback_internal, fan_pwm variance detected. event_id=evt_2026_03_18_0613
Kevin: Can you paste the nvml output from that host?
Maya: quick paste:```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,power.draw,clocks.sm --format=csv
0, A100-80GB, 82 C, 310.2 W, 1095 MHz
1, A100-80GB, 44 C, 120.5 W, 930 MHz
```
Maya: card 0 is pegged and temps oscillate by ~6-8C in 30s windows.
Aj: hmm, why is power.draw > 300W on an 80GB? Is power cap disabled?
Maya: power_cap reports as 0 (unlimited) for that GPU.
SRE-oncall: dmesg from node shows PSU handoff messages.```
Mar 18 06:11:42 kernel: pcie-0: ASIC: 12V rail sag detected, delta=-0.32V
Mar 18 06:11:42 kernel: psu-controller: handoff from PSU-A to PSU-B, transient_correction=0.28V
Mar 18 06:12:03 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: Xid 13 (CE) 0x00000000
Mar 18 06:12:05 kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: ECC: single-bit error corrected
```
Kevin: Xid 13 + ECC corrections + rail sag. That aligns with driver throttling and NVML reporting.
Rachel: Could be PSU switchover causing momentary undervolt -> GPU clocks spike then thermal response -> fans jitter. I've seen that cause evictions in other fleets.
Aj: Immediate mitigation: set a conservative power cap on GPU0 and drain pods using it.
Maya: running drain now: `./infra/drain_node.sh node-gpu-42 --reason "thermal/rail-handoff"`
infra-bot: Drain started for node-gpu-42. Pods: 12 affected. ETA ~6m.
SRE-oncall: Also toggling governor to limit max clocks until hardware swap. `echo 900 > /sys/class/drm/card0/device/pp_dpm_sclk_max` (doing via runbook).
Kevin: Can we enable NVML persistence to capture pre/post handoff counters?
Aj: enabled persistence and increased driver logging to debug for that host. Collecting /var/log/messages and kernel ring for 24h.
Maya: After drain, tail-latency returned to normal. We lost ~6 GPUs of effective capacity during remediation window.
Rachel: Ops plan: schedule PSU module warm-swap and replace thermal paste on that node tomorrow. Also run a quick fan PWM calibration to remove micro-jitter.
Aj: Who's owning the swap?
Maya: @Rachel will coordinate with colo. She already opened ticket with vendor: TKT-9921.
Rachel: Yep, vendor ETA 10:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll also tag spare card for testing if swap doesn't fix it.
SRE-oncall: Follow-ups: (1) add alert for sensor-failover -> automatic soft-powercap set (2) add metric for rail-voltage-sags to perf dashboard (3) run fleet-wide check for PSU firmware versions.
Kevin: Agree. Also add an automated drain policy when Xid+rail-sag co-occur within 2m.
Maya: Filed infra issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4217 (notes + logs attached).
Aj: Nice catch. Lessons: sensor failover masks ambient readings, PSU handoffs can cause short undervolt that manifests as thermal + ECC noise, and that cascades into inference tail-latency.
Maya: Closing thread once swap confirmed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
